title: Preregistered paired evaluation of generate→verify→repair (G→V→R) vs LLM‑only NetOps suggestions
research_question: To what extent does an iterative generate→verify→repair pipeline reduce regression‑causing network changes compared to an LLM‑only suggestion pipeline, and what are the cost/latency tradeoffs?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1 (confirmatory): The G→V→R pipeline yields a lower regression‑causing change rate (proportion of tasks with failed post‑apply regression tests) than the LLM‑only pipeline (paired estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline).
exploratory_questions: Do verifier‑only blocking and repair‑without‑verifier ablations explain the mechanism of any observed improvement?
How does time‑to‑deploy and model‑call cost per successful apply trade off against regression reduction?
Are residual regressions concentrated on particular vendor/feature clusters?
benchmark_scope: Public topology + change‑intent corpus assembled deterministically from public datasets referenced in evidence_record_ids.
Included tasks limited to intents where the preregistered verifier reports feature/protocol coverage (verifier coverage matrix preregistered).
primary_estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (absolute difference in regression‑causing change rate: G→V→R minus LLM‑only, paired within task)
sampling_plan: Deterministic selection from the assembled public change‑intent pool: (1) assemble candidate list from cited public corpora; (2) filter to intents covered by preregistered verifier; (3) compute SHA‑256(intent_string) and sort ascending; (4) select first K=200 tasks. Excluded intents (verifier/validation failures or duplicate hashes) are logged with automated reasons and placed in an exclusions manifest. No human selection or annotation.
power_and_precision_plan: Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Target effect: absolute reduction 0.08 (from 0.20 to 0.12). Two‑sided alpha=0.05, power=0.80. Primary power check: approximate paired‑proportion normal calculation cross‑checked with preregistered Monte‑Carlo bootstrap simulation (10,000 runs) on CPU using the registered analysis executor. Sensitivity analyses vary baseline across {0.10,0.15,0.20,0.25,0.30} and recompute power; bootstrap CI stability checks at 5k and 20k resamples.
exclusion_rules: Tasks excluded automatically if verifier coverage or transformation semantic_equivalence checks fail; reason logged.
Tasks excluded if deterministic hash duplicate detected between intents/prompts; reason logged.
Tasks excluded if API headers indicate irrecoverable stateful behavior after the preregistered automatic retry procedure; reason logged.
missingness_plan: Primary treatment 'complete_pair_primary': pairs where both arms fail to produce an interpretable apply (e.g., emulator fatal error) are recorded and excluded from primary analysis; counts and reasons reported. Sensitivity analyses treat any missing/failed arm as a regression failure (complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity). All missingness and exclusion reasons are fully logged; no human adjudication.
analysis_plan: Primary confirmatory analysis executed by 'paired_binary_analysis_v1' computing paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline on K=200 paired tasks. Primary test: paired/paired‑proportion test (McNemar or equivalent) with bootstrap (10,000 resamples) for 95% CI. Secondary analyses: Kaplan‑Meier for time‑to‑successful‑apply with log‑rank test (right‑censor at max iterations), subgroup descriptive analyses by preregistered vendor/feature clusters with Holm correction. All analysis code, seeds, and executor identifiers preregistered and versioned; analyses executed on CPU.
multiplicity_plan: Primary hypothesis H1 is the single preregistered confirmatory test (alpha=0.05). Secondary and subgroup analyses are exploratory; reported p‑values adjusted using Holm method. All planned comparisons enumerated in analysis code; unplanned comparisons labeled exploratory.
contamination_plan: Risk factors: duplicate/near‑duplicate intents, hosted model training overlap with public corpora (residual uncertainty), and stateful API behavior. Detection: deterministic SHA‑256 hashing of intents/prompts and per‑call prompt/response hash logging; per‑call API header logging for stateful signatures. Rules: duplicates or matching response hashes automatically flagged and excluded from confirmatory sample; calls with stateful headers retried once under a cleared session, then excluded if repeated. Analysis treatment: automatically flagged items excluded from primary analysis; sensitivity analyses treat flagged items as failures and report deduplicated-inclusion results. Residual uncertainty (training overlap, nondetectable server nondeterminism) is documented and quantified via a reserved verification subset (N=10) with repeated calls.
stopping_rule: Stop after processing and recording results for all K=200 confirmatory paired tasks or upon exceeding the preregistered maximum_model_calls=400, or upon an unrecoverable provider/infrastructure failure that aborts the run; automated per-task retry budget applied as preregistered (single automatic retry for stateful calls). Any early stop and reason are logged and reported.
planned_outputs: IEEE two‑column LaTeX manuscript (≤5 pages) and compiled PDF
Analysis code and paired_binary_analysis_v1 execution log
Raw model prompts/responses, hashes, and artifacts
Failure analysis record and evidence‑to‑claim table
